zones.label: Water
zones.summary: Water is the best everyday choice for replacing fluid.
facts: Water has no added sugar or caffeine.
Bodies need water before, during, and after active play.
Thirst is one clue, but drinking regularly helps before thirst grows strong.

zones.label: Nourishing Drinks
zones.summary: Plain milk and culturally familiar unsweetened alternatives can add nutrients as well as fluid.
facts: Plain milk contains natural sugar rather than added sweetener.
Nourishing alternatives vary by family and culture.
A trusted adult can help compare an unfamiliar drink.

zones.label: Sugary Drinks
zones.summary: Some drinks contain a large amount of added sugar even when they look fruity or sporty.
facts: Added sugar can contribute to tooth decay.
A sweet drink may give quick energy followed by a tired feeling.
These drinks are not needed for ordinary everyday hydration.

zones.label: Caffeinated Drinks
zones.summary: Caffeine can affect a child’s sleep, heart rate, and calm focus.
facts: Caffeine may be found in energy drinks, some sodas, and some teas.
Children are more sensitive to caffeine than adults.
Ask a trusted adult to help read an unfamiliar label.
